html:
SMTO-HTTP-0074 — A saved sign-in can't add its details to this request

GUID: a3b1f73f-fadc-4b5f-9757-ed7b25702aab
Slug: http-session-body-invalid
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • This saved connection signs in and then adds a sign-in value to each request's data. This request's data had no place to put it, so the request was not sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select the saved HTTP Connection, and open Advanced login settings. Find the Extracted value whose Destination is body. That rule is the one trying to add the sign-in value into the request's data.
  2. If the service accepts it, change that Destination to header, cookie or query, or list only the methods that need it in Methods (comma separated). Then save. A header, cookie or web address part can carry the value no matter what kind of data the request sends.
  3. If the value must stay in the data, ask SMTO in the conversation to send the request as a form or as named fields. The sign-in value can only be added to form data or a set of named fields, not to plain text or a list.

What success looks like

  • The request is sent and the step shows the service's reply instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up this connection. Don't paste the sign-in value into the conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • SessionLogin.prepare_request could not inject an extracted session value into the body because the body is not a JSON object or its media type is neither application/json nor form-urlencoded.

What this means

  • Session field injection encounters a JSON body that is not an object or a media type other than supported JSON/form data. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Session field injection encounters a JSON body that is not an object or a media type other than supported JSON/form data.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare injection target rules with the request's actual object/form body and media type.

How to fix it

  • For session_login profiles with an extraction rule whose target is body, send a JSON object or form-urlencoded body on matching methods, or change that rule's target to header, cookie or query, or restrict its methods. Rules live under auth.login extract in the saved HTTP profile.
  • Use the configured JSON/form object body or correct the session injection configuration for the endpoint.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Required session fields are injected into the documented supported body representation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
